top_story.headline: Khanna and Massie file war powers resolution to end U.S. hostilities against Houthis in Yemen
top_story.dek: The House met for two minutes of business on Friday, but a bipartisan war powers measure was among 31 items introduced.
paragraphs: Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), joined by Rep. Thomas Massie, introduced H.Con.Res. 124, a concurrent resolution directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Houthis in Yemen that have not been authorized by Congress. It was referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

The resolution invokes the War Powers Resolution’s provision on removing forces from unauthorized hostilities. The Congressional Record text shows only the referral; no floor vote or scheduling was recorded on Friday, when the House adjourned until 1:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13, 2026.
No new Congressional Record issue has been published since this one (first covered 2026-10-10); the summary below is carried over.

sections.headline: Pro forma sessions in both chambers; 31 House measures introduced
paragraphs: Both chambers held brief sessions on Friday, October 9, 2026, with no votes. The Senate met in pro forma session at 1:30 p.m. and adjourned 38 seconds later until 3:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13. The House met at 12:30 p.m. and adjourned at 12:32 p.m. until 1:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13. No committee hearings were held, and the Record lists no Senate bills.

The House received 27 bills, one concurrent resolution and three simple resolutions. Beyond the war powers measure, items drawing attention include a bipartisan 340B rebate limit, a Federal Trade Commission whistleblower bill, a ban on holding certain whales and dolphins for public display, and a resolution on Columbus monuments. Every measure introduced is listed below.

items: H.R. 10768, sponsored by Rep. Tom Barrett (R-MI-7) — would create an Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10769, sponsored by Rep. Everton Blair (D-GA-13) — would let certain facilities be placed within the right-of-way of any federally aided highway; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10770, sponsored by Rep. Robert P. Bresnahan (R-PA-8) — would temporarily limit the use of rebates under the 340B drug discount program; cosponsored by Rep. Debbie Dingell and Rep. Lois Frankel among others; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10771, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — would create an emergency preparedness grant program for higher education institutions; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
H.R. 10772, sponsored by Rep. Jim Costa (D-CA-21) — would evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10773, sponsored by Rep. Jeff Crank (R-CO-5) — would amend the Internal Revenue Code to prevent governmental interference in the operation of private and religious schools; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10774, sponsored by Rep. Suzan K. DelBene (D-WA-1) — would prohibit the taking, importation, exportation and breeding of certain cetaceans (whales and dolphins) for public display, amending the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 and the Animal Welfare Act; carries 23 Democratic cosponsors named in the Record; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources and, additionally, the Committee on Agriculture.

H.R. 10775, sponsored by Rep. Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA-10) — would direct the Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission to set up a task force studying the effects of automated accounts on social media, public discourse and elections; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10776, sponsored by Rep. Mike Ezell (R-MS-4) — would change requirements for the allowed take of marine mammals under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10777, sponsored by Rep. Pat Fallon (R-TX-4) — would codify certain policies to combat transnational cyber-enabled crime; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, with the Committees on Homeland Security and Foreign Affairs also assigned.

H.R. 10778, sponsored by Rep. Valerie P. Foushee (D-NC-4) — would create a tax credit for health care facilities that use certain low-emission anesthetic gases; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10779, sponsored by Rep. Andrew R. Garbarino (R-NY-2) — would name the Postal Service facility at 1905 Route 112 in Medford, New York, the “Gunnery Sergeant Ruben Santos Post Office Building”; 12 cosponsors from the New York delegation; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.R. 10780, sponsored by Rep. Jared F. Golden (D-ME-2) — would modify and enhance the federal budgeting and appropriations process; cosponsored by Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez among others; referred to the Committee on Rules with four other committees also assigned.

H.R. 10781, sponsored by Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-FL-8) — would request the President to designate a month each year as National American History and Founders Month; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
H.R. 10782, sponsored by Rep. Jahana Hayes (D-CT-5) — would reauthorize the Clean School Bus Program; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10783, sponsored by Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC-1) — would provide for payment of attorney’s fees to a prevailing defendant in a civil action for defamation or libel; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10784, sponsored by Rep. Richard McCormick (R-GA-7) — would amend the Internal Revenue Code to provide home ownership assistance; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means and, additionally, the Committee on Financial Services.
H.R. 10785, sponsored by Rep. Analilia Mejia (D-NJ-11) — would reauthorize the SCORE small-business mentoring program under the Small Business Act; referred to the Committee on Small Business.

H.R. 10786, sponsored by Rep. Max L. Miller (R-OH-7) — would require certain colleges to make U.S.-citizen students pass the United States naturalization test to graduate; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.R. 10787, sponsored by Rep. Gregory F. Murphy (R-NC-3) — would exclude urological and ostomy supplies from Medicare competitive acquisition programs for 5 years; cosponsored by Rep. Brad Schneider; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10788, sponsored by Rep. Frank Pallone (D-NJ-6) — the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act, which would adjust surprise medical billing requirements for private health insurance; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce with two other committees also assigned.

H.R. 10789, sponsored by Rep. Jimmy Patronis (R-FL-1) — would establish a moratorium on oil and gas production and exploration in the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range; nine Florida Republican cosponsors named in the Record; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10790, sponsored by Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D-WA-3) — would require that at least one member of the Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board have demonstrated knowledge and substantial experience in the trades or industrial labor; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10791, sponsored by Rep. Michael A. Rulli (R-OH-6) — would bar federal funds to any state or local government that celebrates Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.R. 10792, sponsored by Rep. Janice D. Schakowsky (D-IL-9) — would provide incentives for and protect whistleblowers under the authority of the Federal Trade Commission; cosponsored by Rep. Lori Trahan among others; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and, additionally, the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10793, sponsored by Rep. Derek Schmidt (R-KS-2) — would modify the Department of Defense’s authority for installation support services and intergovernmental support agreements; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10794, sponsored by Rep. Norma J. Torres (D-CA-35) — would create a grant program helping states improve access to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC); 22 cosponsors named in the Record; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.Con.Res. 124, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — would direct the President, under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against the Houthis in Yemen that Congress has not authorized; cosponsored by Rep. Thomas Massie; referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.Res. 1621, sponsored by Rep. J. Luis Correa (D-CA-46) — would express profound sorrow over the death of Alexander Michel Odeh; cosponsored by Rep. Rashida Tlaib; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.Res. 1622, sponsored by Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24) — would express support for preserving, protecting and maintaining statues and monuments honoring Christopher Columbus; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.
H.Res. 1623, sponsored by Rep. Bruce Westerman (R-AR-4) — would recognize October 2026 as “National Dyslexia Awareness Month”; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.
